skill.name: email-sequence
skill.description: Designs lifecycle email sequences with defined triggers, timing, audience segments, persuasive copy, calls to action, testing plans, and performance metrics.
skill.summary: Create structured email campaigns for onboarding, nurture, retention, billing, re-engagement, and product updates.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 13 static findings are false positives. The command findings are Markdown fences, while the reconnaissance findings are ordinary email marketing prose with no executable or probing behavior.

Lines 893-896 only close one Markdown fence and open another around an email format example. No command or interpreter invocation is present.
Lines 896-904 are a fenced output template containing email fields and placeholders. The fence is documentation syntax, not executable backtick substitution.
Line 84 advises B2B marketers to avoid weekend sends. It does not inspect a system or collect host information.
Lines 297-298 define an email trigger and retention goal after a user becomes a paying customer. This is lifecycle marketing logic, not system reconnaissance.
Line 303 schedules an email about paid product features. It contains no host discovery, system query, or executable instruction.
Lines 348-349 are a heading and marketing trigger for an upgrade campaign. They do not request or expose system information.
Lines 350-351 state the conversion goal and expected email count. This is campaign planning without system inspection behavior.
Line 751 is an audit checklist item for an upgrade email sequence. It neither discovers system details nor directs a tool to run.
Lines 847-848 list customer lifecycle segments such as trial, paid, new, and long-term. These are marketing audiences, not system targets.
Lines 48-49 advise leading emails with useful content to build trust. No network address, scan, request, or discovery action appears.
Lines 122-123 describe helping recipients achieve a small success. This is copy strategy and contains no network reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Disconnected emails weaken engagement and conversion. This skill designs targeted lifecycle sequences with clear triggers, timing, copy, calls to action, and measurement plans.
actual_capabilities: Plans welcome, onboarding, nurture, retention, billing, win-back, and campaign sequences.
Defines entry triggers, send timing, exit conditions, audience segments, and conversion goals.
Writes subject lines, preview text, email bodies, and focused calls to action.
Suggests behavioral personalization, segmentation rules, and coordinated lifecycle messaging.
Creates testing and measurement plans for engagement, conversion, retention, and revenue metrics.
limitations: It does not send emails or configure an email service provider.
It needs product, audience, offer, brand voice, and campaign goal details for tailored output.
It does not verify legal compliance, consent records, deliverability settings, or data privacy controls.
Its performance benchmarks are directional and require validation against your audience and historical results.

use_cases.title: Launch a Welcome Journey
use_cases.description: Create a timed welcome series that delivers an immediate benefit, builds trust, and guides new subscribers toward one conversion goal.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Adoption
use_cases.description: Design behavior-based onboarding emails that support setup, highlight useful features, and help users reach meaningful product milestones.

use_cases.title: Recover Inactive Customers
use_cases.description: Plan a respectful re-engagement or win-back sequence using past value, relevant updates, feedback requests, and clear exit conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Welcome Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five-email welcome sequence for [product] aimed at [audience]. Include timing, subject lines, preview text, body copy, and one CTA.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Lead Nurture Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a seven-email lead nurture sequence for [offer]. Move [audience] from [current awareness] to [conversion goal] over [timeframe].
prompt_templates.scenario: Educate prospects before a sales offer.

prompt_templates.title: Segment an Onboarding Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Create onboarding branches for active, stalled, and inactive [product] users. Define behavior triggers, delays, exit conditions, copy goals, and success metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Optimize a Lifecycle Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the attached email program against lifecycle coverage, relevance, timing, personalization, and measurement. Prioritize gaps and propose an A/B testing roadmap.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an established multi-stage email program.

output_examples.input: Create a three-email welcome sequence for a team planning application.
output: Email 1 sends immediately, welcomes the user, and links to project creation.
Email 2 sends after one day and helps the user invite a teammate.
Email 3 sends after three days and shows how a similar team reached its first milestone.

output_examples.input: Plan a re-engagement campaign for subscribers inactive for 60 days.
output: Start with a direct check-in and one useful reason to return.
Follow with relevant product updates and a low-friction action.
End with a clear preference choice and remove unresponsive recipients from the sequence.

best_practices: Provide a specific audience, trigger, conversion goal, offer, and brand voice before requesting copy.
Use one primary job and one primary call to action for each email.
Validate timing, consent, personalization data, links, and exit conditions before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not combine several unrelated goals or competing calls to action in one email.
Do not use fabricated urgency, unsupported claims, or personalization data that recipients did not provide.
Do not send every sequence to the full list without segmentation, suppression rules, or frequency controls.

faq.question: Can this skill write complete email copy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce subject lines, preview text, body copy, calls to action, timing, and segment conditions.

faq.question: Which email sequence types are supported?
faq.answer: It covers welcome, onboarding, nurture, retention, billing, usage, win-back, newsletter, promotion, and product update sequences.

faq.question: Does it connect to an email platform?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategy and copy but does not configure, send, or monitor campaigns in an email service.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, entry trigger, desired action, product value, objections, brand voice, offer details, and current performance.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing sequence?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the current sequence and metrics to receive a gap analysis, revised structure, copy recommendations, and test priorities.

faq.question: Does it guarantee legal compliance or performance?
faq.answer: No. Review consent, privacy, unsubscribe, and advertising requirements locally, then test recommendations against your own audience data.
